name: Barabbas
summary: A notable prisoner, lying bound with them that had made insurrection and had committed murder in the insurrection. Pilate offered the crowd a choice between him and Jesus; the chief priests moved them to ask for Barabbas. He was released and Jesus was crucified.
offense: Rebellion against the government and murder, both capital under the law of Moses and of Rome. Peter states the exchange to the men of Israel: ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you.
judgment: Released, by the custom of the feast and the demand of the crowd. The guilty man walked free because the innocent was condemned in his place; the gospels leave the figure there and say no more of him.

entries.commentary: They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

Peter and John go up to the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. Counting the way the scripture counts, the day starts at six in the morning: six is the start, so the third hour is nine in the morning, the sixth hour is noon, and the ninth hour is three in the afternoon. Write that down, because knowing how the hours are counted keeps you from being confused later.

A certain man, lame from his mother's womb, is carried and laid daily at the gate called Beautiful to ask alms of those going into the temple. He sees Peter and John about to go in and asks alms, expecting to receive something. This is how you know these are our people, because you primarily see our people begging on the streets, laid low and asking for alms.

Peter says, "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk." This is why, when people at camp ask if we give money to the poor, we say no. A lot of times we do not know why the Most High put a person in that condition, and the money could end up feeding a drug dealer, a drug addict, or a child molester without our knowing it. The Most High is the one who brings a man low. Sometimes he withholds money, status, or a job to hinder a man from sinning, the way he removed King Manasseh from his power. Many hurtful lusts come from the love of money, and celebrities get caught up in wickedness because riches in the hand of a man who has sin become a tool for evil. He wants to teach you discipline and contentment first, so that when the money comes it is only a tool to pay your bills and support the truth, not to live in the delicacies of this life. -

Peter takes him by the right hand and lifts him up, and immediately his feet and ankle bones receive strength, and he stands, leaps, walks, and enters the temple praising the Most High. Everything the apostles did was prepared and taught to them; they did not move independently. We cannot heal a body today, but we heal every day with the word: drug dealers, baby mothers, and survivors of mental, physical, alcoholic, drug, and religious abuse are healed when they receive the truth. When people say we do not feed the poor, the truth is the poor have the gospel preached to them, and that is the healing. -

All the people see him walking and praising the Most High, know he is the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful gate, and are filled with wonder, running together to Peter and John at the porch called Solomon's. Notice it says "all the people," because a book establishes its characters at the start and then speaks in pronouns, "he," "she," "they," "all," without re-naming the people every time. Christians, and primarily our own people because of a lack of education and reading comprehension, have forgotten who "all the people" are. You have to be war-minded and read into the context so you know the audience, because the verse always clears up who is being addressed, if not in the same verse then in the next. Even in the world, our people who deny the truth get quiet when the scriptures are laid out and the black image of Christ is shown from the Bible, and some wake up on the spot and say, "It is in the Bible, I respect it," which is the spirit of the Most High coming upon them.

When Peter sees it he answers, "Ye men of Israel, why marvel ye at this? or why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" This is the verse that establishes the audience: the "all the people" of verse 11 are the men of Israel. The healing was not by Peter's own power or holiness. He was not God for doing the work, any more than Elijah was God for raising the dead; it was done by the power of the Most High. This is why the book of Acts is so important, because if you get well versed in Acts you can spiritually kill the white supremacist doctrine and the wicked Christian mindset that has been planted in our people's minds.

Peter names "the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers," who glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up and denied before Pilate when Pilate was determined to let him go. The oath and promise passed through a royal lineage: Abraham had Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, but Ishmael was rejected and Isaac was chosen. If the covenant were for all nations, it would have passed through Ishmael too, but it went straight down to Isaac, showing this is not the God of all nations but the God of our fathers.

They denied the Holy One and the Just and desired a murderer to be granted to them, and killed the Prince of life, whom the Most High raised from the dead, of which the apostles are witnesses. Christians claim the new covenant opened salvation to everybody once Christ died, but the text keeps the promise on the same people.

It is his name, through faith in his name, that made this man strong, and the faith which is by him gave the man this perfect soundness in the presence of them all. The strength did not come from the men but from faith in the name of Christ.

Peter says, "And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it, as did also your rulers," but the things the Most High showed before by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he has so fulfilled. Christ fulfilled his suffering; he did not do away with the law and the prophets. If you claim Christ suffered and died for all nations, prove it "by the mouth of all his prophets." Show it through Isaiah, Ezekiel, Jeremiah, or Haggai, that Christ suffered and died for all nations, because the text says all his prophets foretold it. -

"Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord." People say they repented without understanding the scriptural meaning of the words. To repent is to turn from all your transgressions, and to be converted is to change, which requires the law to change to. -

"And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you." The "you" is Israel, which was established back in verse 12, so you have to read the whole chapter as one audience being addressed.

"Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began." Restitution is the restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner, the same word used when land seized from our people is demanded back. We are living the restitution of all things right now, before Christ comes. To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored. -

"For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things," and every soul that will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people. The prophet is raised up "from among their brethren," meaning from among men, which proves Christ came through the seed of a man, not immaculate conception. Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept. -

"Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days." All the prophets from Samuel onward foretold these days, tying back to the "you" who are the men of Israel established in verse 12.

"Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations. -

"Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities." "Unto you first" means unto Judah, the Jews first, and the "you" being turned from iniquities is Israel, the same audience throughout the chapter. There was an order and prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, the "Jews," and the "Jew and Gentile" and "Jew and Greek" language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes; the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved. -

The fining pot and furnace remove impurities from silver and gold; likewise the Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities. We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom. This is why Christianity is false when it teaches you only have to accept Jesus in your heart to be saved forever. That is not what the scriptures say. Whoso mocks the poor reproaches his Maker, and gladness at another man's calamity does not go unpunished. Children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers. Many of us grew up in fatherless homes, but we must not glory in a father's dishonor. Sisters should not speak evil of the man they chose to lie down with and bring in seed by, no matter how bad he is; children raised to despise their fathers must repent of it in this truth. Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness. -

A gift is as a precious stone to him that has it; a well-instructed wife is one of these gifts, silent and loving, priceless and far above rubies. A silent and loving woman does not mean one who never talks; it means a shamefaced sister who is not a chest bumper, whose continent mind cannot be valued. He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned. -

A reproof enters more into a wise man than a hundred stripes into a fool; the wise receive correction while the fool must be beaten. Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house. That is everything right there. The beginning of strife is like letting out water, so leave off contention before it is meddled with; where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work. Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart. -

He that justifies the wicked and he that condemns the just are both an abomination to the Most High. To justify the wicked is to wrest judgment and take a bribe. A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous, and this perverting of judgment is something we suffer with as a people. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who justify the wicked for reward; the reward usually comes as a financial gift or a place of importance. There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it. -

A friend loves at all times and a brother is born for adversity; a man void of understanding strikes hands and becomes surety before his friend. He that loves transgression loves strife, and he that exalts his gate seeks destruction; a froward heart finds no good and a perverse tongue falls into mischief.

A foolish son is grief to his father; Solomon understood the reasonings of men, which is why a wicked man takes a gift from the bosom to pervert judgment appears again and again in this one chapter. A merry heart does good like a medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones. Wisdom is before him that has understanding, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth. Understanding comes only through keeping the commandments. This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man. -

A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to his mother; to punish the just and strike princes for equity is not good. He that has knowledge spares his words, and even a fool who holds his peace is counted wise. Talking too much, especially without the words of the Most High, marks a fool. Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words; speak only when there is need of thee and hold thy tongue among great men. -

verses.text: Now at that feast he released unto them one prisoner, whomsoever they desired.
And there was one named Barabbas, which lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.
And the multitude crying aloud began to desire him to do as he had ever done unto them.
But Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.
But the chief priests moved the people, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.
And Pilate answered and said again unto them, What will ye then that I shall do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?
And they cried out again, Crucify him.
Then Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? And they cried out the more exceedingly, Crucify him.
And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.
And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas:
(Who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.)
And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.
Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.
And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?
For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.
When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.
But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
But ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you;
He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the Lord.
